sources.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs

The extraction limitation was addressed by visual inspection of PDF pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12 and 14 and all six final crops. Other pages were read as complete extracted text; their figure images were not visually inspected.
The submitted reproducibility archive, code, weights and separate media were not supplied or inspected; no experiments were reproduced.

Identity matches the catalog: the observed title and all eight authors agree. The inspected artifact is arXiv:2608.02578v1 [cs.RO], 3 August 2026. No other revision or edition was supplied or compared.

synopsis: CoWAM uses typed coordination obligations and calibrated future evidence to decide whether an existing bimanual policy action should change. Its frozen proposer supplies alternatives; the selector cannot invent missing actions. Outcome-blind comparisons report better coordination selection and simulated closed-loop completion, while conservative gates limit unsupported overrides.

problem.text: A plausible predicted rollout can conceal mistimed contacts, incompatible arm roles or converging collisions. CoWAM asks when predicted consequences justify replacing Policy Top-1, balancing coordination repairs against damage to an already valid nominal action.

contributions.text: Coordination contracts combine noncompensable typed predicates, event-conditioned learned evidence and calibrated intervention gates.
An outcome-blind same-pool protocol separates selection quality from the availability of successful proposals, with simulator labels obtained only after selectors commit.

inputs: Current multi-view observation and task-phase/event state
An ordered pool of synchronized left-right action chunks, four-step predicted RGB-D futures and predicted proprioception
outputs: Preserve the nominal action, override with an eligible existing candidate, or invoke the task-defined abstention fallback
A committed record of candidate identities, contract outcomes, scores, bounds and decision mode

steps.name: Freeze the proposal interface
steps.detail: At each replanning step, preserve candidate identities and order; index zero is nominal. The primary proposer is X-WAM. CoWAM neither resamples candidates nor updates the proposer.

steps.name: Activate coordination obligations
steps.detail: Task phase activates synchronization, role compatibility and collision-convergence predicates. Contact order, grasp ownership, separation and approach trends supply typed evidence. Every active obligation must pass; unrelated utility cannot compensate for a failure.

steps.name: Estimate future-dependent evidence
steps.detail: Three independently seeded verifiers consume observation, action, predicted future and event type. Heads estimate satisfaction, risk, utility, opportunity and confidence. Ensemble dispersion makes risk more pessimistic and utility less optimistic.

steps.name: Qualify and execute
steps.detail: An alternative must pass contract, risk, utility-retention, opportunity, event-confidence and score-margin gates. Choose the highest-scoring eligible alternative, breaking ties by proposer order. Otherwise preserve a contract-valid nominal candidate or use the frozen fallback, then replan.

training.text: The policy and WAM remain frozen. Table A2 specifies three verifier instances, a 60/20/20 train/validation/test split by task-seed group, AdamW at 3×10⁻⁴, batch 128 and 100 epochs. Appendix A identifies 1,200 test groups containing 9,600 candidate records. Calibration and normalization are frozen before evaluation.
The PDF does not specify the verifier backbone, complete loss functions or loss weights. It lists output targets and optimization settings, which are insufficient to reconstruct training exactly.

inference.text: Default settings include eight candidates, risk threshold 0.20, utility lower floor 0.55, selective margin 0.12, event confidence 0.70 and enabled abstention. The text does not fully map the tabulated absolute utility floor onto the nominal-relative inequality.

The online selector uses predicted evidence, not future simulator outcomes. Shared oracle execution labels candidates afterward for task success, coordination, progress and failure mode; oracle performance is an offline proposal ceiling.

equations.explanation: Equation (2): the event vocabulary is \(\mathcal E\); \(m_{t,e}\) activates event \(e\), and \(c_{i,e}\) is candidate \(i\)'s binary predicate. Thus \(g_i\) requires every active predicate.

equations.expression: R_i^{+}=\bar r_i+\kappa_r s_i^r,\qquad U_i^{-}=\bar u_i-\kappa_u s_i^u,\qquad S_i=U_i^{-}+\lambda_o\hat o_i-\lambda_r R_i^{+}
equations.explanation: Equations (4–5): bars are ensemble means; \(s_i^r,s_i^u\) measure predictive dispersion. Frozen multipliers \(\kappa_r,\kappa_u\) form risk/utility bounds. Score \(S_i\) rewards utility and estimated opportunity \(\hat o_i\), and penalizes risk through nonnegative weights.

Equation (6): indicators enforce risk threshold \(\tau_r\), tolerated utility loss \(\epsilon_u\), opportunity threshold \(\tau_o\), confidence threshold \(\tau_q\) and margin \(\tau_m\). \(Q_i\) is minimum satisfaction confidence over active events; subscript zero denotes the nominal candidate. \(G_i=1\) authorizes an override.

results.task: Natural closed-loop success across eight RoboTwin 2.0 tasks
results.setting: 30 paired held-out seeds per task; 240 simulated episodes per method; strict simulator completion within a fixed horizon.
results.metric: Task success; coordination validity; false/harmful intervention rates
results.value: 151/240 successes (62.9%); 95.4% coordination validity; 3.3% false and 0.4% harmful intervention.
results.comparison: Selective Control: 128/240 (53.3%); Policy Top-1: 96/240 (40.0%); offline oracle: 176/240 (73.3%).
results.interpretation: The reported gain over Selective Control is 9.6 percentage points, with 32 versus 9 discordant pairs and reported exact paired p=4.3×10⁻⁴. Each task improves by 1–4 episodes; physical-robot transfer is untested.

results.setting: 180 event-stress clusters across eight tasks; 150 oracle-confirmed opportunities and 180 matched contract-valid negatives.
results.metric: Valid selection on positives; false/harmful intervention on negatives
results.interpretation: The 16.7-point gain over Contract-only has 27 versus 2 discordant pairs (reported p=1.6×10⁻⁶). Family counts are 47/50, 46/50 and 47/50. These opportunity-conditioned rates are distinct from episode success.

results.setting: The same 150 positive and 180 matched-negative units as the coordination audit.
results.comparison: No uncertainty bound: 94.7% / 14.4% / 3.3%; no baseline preservation: 96.7% / 28.9% / 7.8%.
results.interpretation: Higher positive selection alone favors permissive variants; matched-negative errors expose the cost. Contract-only removes both learned evidence and gates, so it is not an isolated test of event conditioning.

results.setting: 1,200 task-seed-disjoint test groups; 9,600 correlated candidate records.
results.metric: AUPRC; pair accuracy; expected calibration error
results.interpretation: Candidate-specific future evidence supports discrimination and calibration in this test distribution; it is not a bound on deployment risk.

results.setting: Retained subsets of the 1,200 ranking groups, reused rather than independent experiments.
results.interpretation: Risk increases as more groups are retained; these rates use retained-group denominators, not the matched-negative denominator.

results.setting: 80 states per candidate count; separately, 120 paired pools per proposer regime over six tasks.
results.metric: Rescues per available opportunity; proposer-conditioned task success
results.value: K=4: 26/28 rescues; K=32: 38/40. X-WAM, LeWorldModel and mixed-pool success: 78/120, 75/120 and 85/120.
results.interpretation: Reported success gains are 10.0, 12.5 and 12.5 percentage points. Reuse of the selector interface does not establish unrestricted transfer to new embodiments.

limitations.text: Evidence is from RoboTwin 2.0 and held-out seeds of the evaluated task definitions. New-task and physical-robot generalization remain open. The oracle–CoWAM success gap also shows residual selection headroom within the fixed proposal pool.

An unresolved ablation discrepancy remains: Table 3 lists no event conditioning at 74.7% valid, 10.0% false and 1.7% harmful; Table A11 lists RGB-D + future, no event at 128/150, 10/180 and 2/180. The source does not explain the configuration difference. Appendix C also says per-task gains are 2–4, while Tables 2/A5 show Scan Object improves by one.

Conservative bounds are empirical ensemble/calibration constructions; the PDF supplies no formal deployment guarantee. Exact predicates, fallback actions, calibration coefficients and several gate settings remain unspecified in the supplied paper.

reproduction.text: Reproduction requires pinned simulator/model revisions, frozen task-seed matrices, ordered candidate-pool digests, committed outcome-blind decisions, shared oracle labels and paired aggregation. The paper says its submitted archive contains these artifacts; their availability is not established by that statement.

Reported selector cost is 88 ms and 4.8 GB on one RTX 5880 Ada, versus 41 ms/3.1 GB for Policy Top-1; offline oracle rollout costs 2,460 ms. Training duration and a complete training-data inventory are not specified.

reasoning.text: The frozen WAM proposer and separate verifier/controller support Dual-system, Other mechanisms and Outside quadrants. CoWAM selects existing action–future pairs; it does not introduce a unified future/action generator or inverse-dynamics action decoder. The post-training tag fits an added learned selector, but the source does not establish policy-weight post-training or reinforcement learning. Generalization evidence is limited to the evaluated regimes.

discussionQuestions: How much of the gate benefit survives when variants are compared at equal override frequency?
Can frozen calibration maintain matched-negative precision under a shift in contact timing or object geometry?
What distinct configurations account for the two no-event ablation results?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author block and left-margin arXiv stamp
evidence.detail: Title matches the supplied observed title. Authors are Shuaijun Liu, Qifu Wen, Shuyang Hao, Qi Luo, Chenglong Zhang, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu and Ningxin Su. Affiliations are HKUST (Guangzhou), Boston University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Stamp: arXiv:2608.02578v1 [cs.RO], 3 Aug 2026.

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Introduction; Figure 1
evidence.detail: Bimanual timing, arm roles, spatial compatibility and phase consistency motivate conservative intervention in nominal policy actions.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 2–3, Figure 2; World-Action Candidate Interface, Eq. (1); p. 9, Decision Procedure
evidence.detail: Frozen ordered action–future pools retain nominal index zero and candidate identities. CoWAM preserves, overrides or abstains without changing the proposer; execution is followed by replanning.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Coordination Contracts, Eq. (2); p. 9, Contract Structure; p. 10, Table A1
evidence.detail: All active synchronization, role and collision predicates must pass. Contract state includes event activation, evidence requirements, thresholds and fallback; inactive events impose no constraint.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Event-Conditioned Contract Evidence, Eqs. (3–5)
evidence.detail: Event-conditioned outputs estimate satisfaction, risk, utility, opportunity and confidence. Ensemble means and dispersion form conservative risk/utility bounds; the frozen score combines utility, opportunity and risk.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Selective Policy Intervention, Eq. (6); p. 9, Decision Procedure
evidence.detail: Contract, risk, utility retention, opportunity, event confidence and margin jointly qualify an alternative. Highest score wins, ties follow proposer order; otherwise preserve a valid nominal action or invoke fallback.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Verifier and Calibration; p. 10, Table A2(a–b)
evidence.detail: Four predicted future steps, three independently seeded verifiers, 60/20/20 task-seed group split, AdamW 3×10⁻⁴, batch 128 and 100 epochs are specified. Defaults are K=8, risk 0.20, utility floor 0.55, margin 0.12, confidence 0.70 and enabled abstention; 1,200 groups/9,600 records are identified as the test block.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, final Methods paragraphs; pp. 9–11, Appendix B, Outcome-Blind Pairing
evidence.detail: Selectors commit identical-pool decisions before shared simulator labeling. Beneficial changes repair a nominal failure without losing a required outcome; harmful changes lose an outcome; false changes lack task/coordination support. Oracle labels are offline.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Experiments—Setup; p. 10, Table A3; p. 11, Metrics and Statistical Tests; p. 16, Table A16
evidence.detail: Eight RoboTwin tasks use 30 natural seeds each. Event audit has 180 clusters, 150 opportunities and 180 matched negatives. Exact paired tests use clusters/episodes, not candidates. Ablations reuse pools; the ledger distinguishes 2,500 independent scientific units from candidate records and timing repetitions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Table 1, CoWAM/Contract-only/RGB-D rows and event-family block; p. 12, Table A6; p. 13, Table A7
evidence.detail: CoWAM records 140/150 valid, 5/180 false and 1/180 harmful; Contract-only 115/150, 20/180, 3/180; RGB-D 126/150, 10/180, 2/180. Family conversions are 47,46,47 of 50. Reported paired discordances are 27 versus 2, p=1.6×10⁻⁶.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Table 2(a–b) and Main Results; p. 12, Table A5
evidence.detail: CoWAM 151/240 successes versus Selective Control 128/240, Policy Top-1 96/240 and oracle 176/240. CoWAM validity/false/harm rates are 95.4%/3.3%/0.4%. Paired discordances 32 versus 9 give reported p=4.3×10⁻⁴. Scan Object rises 17→18; all eight tasks improve.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 3(a) and Ablations discussion
evidence.detail: Full CoWAM valid/false/harm rates are 93.3/2.8/0.6%; removing uncertainty gives 94.7/14.4/3.3%; removing baseline preservation gives 96.7/28.9/7.8%. Contract-only removes learned evidence and gate stack.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 3(b); p. 14, Table A10
evidence.detail: CoWAM AUPRC/AUROC/pair accuracy/ECE/Brier are 0.92/0.96/0.89/0.03/0.07. Scalar AUPRC/pair/ECE are 0.80/0.79/0.06; shuffled futures 0.63/0.62/0.14; current-plus-action AUPRC is 0.75.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Table A14; p. 11, Appendix E, Denominator Ledger
evidence.detail: At 25/50/75/100% coverage, retained N is 300/600/900/1,200; CoWAM violations are 2/7/24/70, reported 0.7/1.2/2.7/5.8%. Future-Consensus has 10/47/131/269. Coverage rows reuse ranking groups.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 4; p. 13, Tables A8–A9; p. 9, Appendix B, Tasks and Evidence Allocation
evidence.detail: K=4/8/16/32 uses 80 states each, opportunities 28/32/36/40 and CoWAM rescues 26/30/34/38. Proposer success is 78/120,75/120,85/120 versus 66/120,60/120,70/120 across X-WAM, LeWorldModel and mixed pools; transfer uses six tasks and 20 seeds per regime.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 3(a), No event conditioning; p. 14, Table A11, RGB-D + future, no event; p. 11, Appendix C, Complete Selector Counts; pp. 5/12, Tables 2/A5, Scan Object
evidence.detail: The no-event rows report 74.7%/10.0%/1.7% versus 128/150,10/180,2/180 without an explicit reconciliation. Appendix C states per-task gains of two to four, but Scan Object improves from 17/30 to 18/30.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Table A13
evidence.detail: Primary proposer is X-WAM; additional proposers are LeWorldModel and mixed pools. The host has eight RTX 5880 Ada GPUs, with one explicitly pinned GPU per job.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Table A15(a–b)
evidence.detail: Per-selection CoWAM latency/memory are 88 ms/4.8 GB, Policy Top-1 41 ms/3.1 GB; offline oracle rollout is 2,460 ms. Failure labels use 240 natural episodes and are non-exclusive.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 11, 14–15, Appendix E, Runtime Environment and Artifacts; Table A13 caption; Claim-Reproduction Order
evidence.detail: The source states a submitted archive contains configurations, revision/checksum references, manifests, decisions, aggregates, statistical scripts and media. It prescribes frozen pools, pre-oracle commitment, shared labeling and paired aggregation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Figure 6 and caption
evidence.detail: Front/head views at initial, middle and terminal stages contrast nominal Place Can in Basket failure with author-labeled successful CoWAM acquisition, transport and placement.
